_comment: AVSET-RESERVE-1. What the engine writes to the log when Reserve capacity runs
on a wave, and what the wave editor makes of it. Decided in TWO places: the
engine (New-VmfWaveReservation) writes the events, the page (reserveScan in
waves.html) reads them. The page used to look for a phrase that only the
claim note carried, so it never saw the answer and said 'still running'.
Its own test fed it an event the engine never wrote.
So this is the one list of cases, and both are held to it:
tests/unit/AvsetReserve.Tests.ps1 runs the engine on each case and compares
every odcr event it writes with 'events'; tests/js/reserve-nothing.test.js
gives the page those same events and checks 'page'.
Only the fields the page reads are compared: step, outcome, code, wave.
'page' is 'nothing' when the log alone answers that the wave has nothing to
reserve, and null when the log does not answer and the claim decides.
'nothingReservable' is what the engine returns for the wave, and 'pill' is
what the wave editor shows for those claims as written, before the run
(loadClaims, then reserveControl): the same rule, decided in both languages.
'plan' is the machines of the wave in the saved plan: in an availability set, or outside one.
_rulesComment: What makes a quota record reservable, decided in Test-VmfClaimReservable
and in the page's claimCount. 'missing' means the field is left out.
Only a whole number says; anything else is not an answer, so reservable.

cases.why: one cell, and every machine in it is in an availability set
two cells, both only availability-set machines
one availability-set cell and one cell Azure reserves - the claim decides, not the log
pressed again after the reservable cell is held - the wave still has something reserved
